extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy and theology; Christian subjects and sovereigns considering duties of obedience and salvation
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance on the relation between civil and ecclesiastical authority, what is necessary for Christian salvation, and how to interpret Scripture in matters of obedience and church power. Focuses on duties of subjects, limits of pastoral power, and criteria for necessary articles of faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of God's command when known
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man receiveth two contrary Commands, and knows that one of them is God's, he ought to obey that, and not the other, though it be the command even of his lawfull Soveraigne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a command is known to be from God, it must be obeyed even against lawful civil commands. The difficulty is often epistemic — knowing whether a command truly comes from God or is only invoked in God's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish necessary vs unnecessary for salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who can distinguish between what is, and what is not Necessary to their Reception into the Kingdome of God, need not be troubled by conflicts between God and civil sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching should enable people to tell whether a civil command can be obeyed without forfeiture of eternal life. If it can be obeyed without eternal loss, disobedience is unjust; if obedience would cause eternal damnation, one must refuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: All that is necessary for salvation: faith and obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is NECESSARY to Salvation, is contained in two Vertues, Faith in Christ, and Obedience to Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faith (belief that Jesus is the Christ) plus the will to obey the Law (repentance/justice) together suffice for salvation; remission of past sins is the reward of faith in Christ. Nothing else is strictly necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal necessary article of faith: Jesus is the Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onely Necessary Article Of Christian Faith ... is this, that JESUS IS THE CHRIST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Evangelists' scope, Apostolic preaching, clear scriptural texts, and examples (e.g., the thief on the cross, John 20:31) are cited to show that believing Jesus is the Christ is sufficient faith for eternal life; other doctrines are implicit or deducible from this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience defined as serious endeavour/will accepted for deed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Obedience required ... that accepteth in all our actions the Will for the Deed, is a serious Endeavour to Obey him; and is called also by all such names as signifie that Endeavour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obedience is sometimes called Charity, Love, Righteousness, Repentance — the internal will to obey suffices because God accepts the will for the deed; perfect external performance is not required for salvation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of divine law: laws of nature and civil law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Laws of God therefore are none but the Laws of Nature, whereof the principall is, that we should not violate our Faith, that is, a commandement to obey our Civill Soveraigns, which wee constituted over us, by mutuall pact one with another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ did not give new civil laws; Scripture mostly counsels observance of existing natural and civil laws. The Bible is law only where the civil sovereign has made it so; elsewhere it is counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for belief: lawful pastors and the supreme pastor
rubrics_metrics.description: The immediate cause of Faith is Hearing ... by Hearing our lawfull Pastors. ... the Person which all they that have no speciall revelation are to beleeve, is (in every Common-wealth) the Supreme Pastor, that is to say, the Civill Soveraigne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary belief in Scripture and doctrine comes from teachers appointed by law (parents, pastors), and ultimate public examination of doctrines belongs to the supreme pastor (civil sovereign). Private claims of revelation are subject to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic principle: interpret by scope not bare words
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the bare Words, but the Scope of the writer that giveth the true light, by which any writing is to bee interpreted; and they that insist upon single Texts, without considering the main Designe, can derive no thing from them cleerly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid atomizing scripture (casting 'atomes of Scripture') and using isolated texts to derive obscure conclusions; prefer the plain and harmonious scope of Scripture when interpreting commands about polity or doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples are weak proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples prove nothing; and the Examples he alledgeth make not so much as a probability of Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on isolated historical examples (e.g., Jehoiada killing Athaliah, Ambrose excommunicating Theodosius) to justify general institutional powers. Example can be misleading or exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of pastoral/ecclesiastical coercive power
rubrics_metrics.description: The Power to Teach ... is no more than the Power, or rather Command to Teach. ... our Saviour refused to take upon him that Power in this world himself, but advised to let the Corn and Tares grow up together till the day of Judgment: much lesse did hee give it to St. Peter, or can S. Peter give it to the Popes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pastoral power consists principally in teaching; it does not, on Scripture grounds, include coercive powers to depose, imprison, or execute Christian kings. Coercive ecclesiastical authority is therefore unjustified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts in one's own cause are void as judicial authority
rubrics_metrics.description: the Judgments are void, as given in their own Cause; and the Acts done by them conformably to this Doctrine, are the greatest Crimes (especially that of Zachary) that are incident to Humane Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a judge or authority acts in their own cause, their judgments lack legitimate authority; such acts should be regarded as void and potentially criminal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other doctrinal articles: necessary if deducible from the foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: They are; and so are many more Articles: but they are such, as are contained in this one, and may be deduced from it, with more, or lesse difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beliefs such as God's omnipotence, resurrection, general resurrection, etc., are necessary insofar as they follow from the foundational belief that Jesus is the Christ; implicit and explicit consequences of the foundation count as part of necessary faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith 'comes by hearing': source and limits of faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith cometh by Hearing, that is, by Hearing our lawfull Pastors. ... the ordinary cause of beleeving that the Scriptures are the Word of God, is the same with the cause of the believing of all other Articles of our Faith, namely, the Hearing of those that are by the Law allowed and appointed to Teach us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal formation of Christian belief is communal and pedagogic; belief is ordinarily formed by lawful teachers rather than private inspiration. This supports deference to established teachers and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When civil sovereign is Christian: obedience compatible with salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whosoever therefore obeyeth his Christian Soveraign, is not thereby hindred, neither from beleeving, nor from obeying God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sovereign is Christian and accepts the foundational faith, his civil laws will ordinarily contain the laws of God; obedience to such a sovereign does not impede salvation. Even if the sovereign errs in consequences, subjects should not presume to judge in matters of obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: When civil sovereign is infidel: do not rebel; faith may be internal
rubrics_metrics.description: And when the Civill Soveraign is an Infidel, every one of his own Subjects that resisteth him, sinneth against the Laws of God ... And for their Faith, it is internall, and invisible; They have the licence that Naaman had, and need not put themselves into danger for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects under an infidel sovereign still ought to obey civil laws; they may keep faith privately and need not provoke persecution or rebellion unless seeking martyrdom for higher spiritual aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of doctrines belongs to supreme pastor
rubrics_metrics.description: there be many false Prophets ... other men are to examine such Spirits (as St. John advised us) 'whether they be of God, or not.' And therefore, seeing the Examination of Doctrines belongeth to the Supreme Pastor, the Person which all they that have no speciall revelation are to beleeve, is ... the Civill Soveraigne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public scrutiny and official adjudication of doctrinal claims should reside with the supreme pastor (civil sovereign/church in commonwealth), not with private individuals; private revelations are subject to such examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of repentance and baptism in salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: Repentance, and Baptisme, that is, beleeving that Jesus Is The Christ, is all that is Necessary to Salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts of repentance (obedience/will) together with confession/baptism grounded in belief that Jesus is the Christ are presented as the practical requirements for receiving remission of sins and the gift of the Holy Ghost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification: how faith and works contribute
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice Justifies in that that sense, in which to Justifie, is the same that to Denominate A Man Just; ... when wee are said to be Justified by Works, it is to be understood of the Will ... And because God accepteth not the Will for the Deed, but onely in the Faithfull; it is therefore Faith that makes good our Plea; and in this sense it is, that Faith onely Justifies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand 'justification by works' as acceptance of the will/endeavour to obey; 'justification by faith' as faith making the will acceptable. Both are necessary but function differently in the doctrine of justification.
